LOOK_AT.say: Pit props holding up the roof.
repeat: I counted the props. I wish I hadn't. I'd have liked a round number.
I tapped one, to see. It's fine. I'm not tapping another.
then: Somebody's carved initials in one, and a date, and lower down, SORRY.

repeat: Wood settling. It's been settling for years, and it's very nearly comfortable.
Quiet. I'm holding my breath, and I think the props are too.

overrides.PULL: No. Not even a little. Not even to see.
overrides.TALK_TO: I thanked them. They hold up a hill all day for nothing, and nobody ever says.

LOOK_AT.say: Daylight, coming down a shaft in the roof in one straight bar.
repeat: There's a disc of sky at the top, the size of a dollar. I know exactly what a dollar looks like. I had four.
A pine needle came down it while I watched, and took its time.
then: The dust in it looks like it's somewhere better.

LISTEN_TO.say: Wind over the top, like breath across a bottle. An F, near enough.
repeat: Birds, far up. Up there it's an ordinary day.
The F again, a hair flat. I can't fix it from down here.

overrides.USE: I stood in it for a minute. It's warm. I'd forgotten the sun was still going on, up there.

exits.name: THE WAY BACK

LOOK_AT.say: Back the way I came, toward the three openings.
repeat: I could go back. I'd only have to come forward again.
Back there the floor was flat and I knew where I was. I've given that up for now.

LISTEN_TO.say: The drip on the stake, faint, behind me.
repeat: Quiet, back there.
A drip, back by the openings.

exits.note: Doc 108: back toward the three openings.

LOOK_AT.say: A passage climbing steeply, with steps cut in it by somebody who hated steps.
repeat: It goes up at an angle a mule would refuse. Grievance was right to stay.
Every step's a different height. Whoever cut them was in a temper, or a hurry, or both.
Still air, up there.
A drip, somewhere up there. Much like down here.

exits.name: THE PASSAGE ON

LOOK_AT.say: A level passage going on into the hill. Easy walking, which makes me suspicious.
repeat: Rails along the floor, rusted to the color of the dark.
Somebody laid rails along it, and never came back for them.
Still air, along there.
A drip along there too. Every passage has one.
